title: Rejetto HTTP File Server RCE
rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Rejetto HFS Command Injection CVE-2014-6287
id: 5a9f3e4d-7b2c-4a8d-9f1e-2c3d4e5f6a7b
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2014-6287 in Rejetto HTTP File Server using null byte injection in the search parameter to execute arbitrary commands. This rule targets the initial access phase where attackers send malicious HTTP requests to the vulnerable service.
references:
    - https://vk9-sec.com/hfs-code-execution-cve-2014-6287/
    - https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/39161
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-29
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1203
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - '%00{.+exec|'
            - 'search=%00{.+exec|'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative tools using similar query patterns
level: high

title: Execution of Commands via Rejetto HFS Exploitation with PowerShell and Netcat
id: 6b8c4f5a-9d7e-3a2b-1c4d-5e6f7a8b9c0d
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of commands through Rejetto HFS vulnerability by monitoring for PowerShell and netcat usage in HTTP request parameters, indicating post-exploitation activities.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-29
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1059.003
logsource:

    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - 'powershell.exe'
            - 'nc.exe'
            - 'http://.*nc.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate network monitoring or diagnostic tools using similar patterns
level: high

id: 308e2f6d-7a4b-4c9e-b1d8-1a0e3f5d7c8a
status: experimental
description: Detects initial access attempts using modified EternalBlue or EternalRomance exploits targeting SMB port 445, which are indicative of WannaCry-style attacks.

status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of rundll32.exe triggered by a user opening an LNK file inside an ISO email attachment, which is a common initial access vector for Ryuk ransomware. title: Initial Access via Oracle EBS CVE-2022-21587 File Upload
id: 3e4b6d9f-2a1c-4b5e-9f8a-1c2d3e4f5a6b
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2022-21587 in Oracle E-Business Suite by monitoring for unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to /OA_HTML/BneOfflineLOVService with UUE encoded ZIP file upload containing path traversal.
references:
    - https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/2023/02/07/etr-cve-2022-21587-rapid7-observed-exploitation-of-oracle-e-business-suite-vulnerability/
    - https://attackerkb.com/topics/Bkij5kK1qK/cve-2022-21587/rapid7-analysis
    - https://github.com/hieuminhnv/CVE-2022-21587-POC
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-29
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection1:
        cs-method: 'POST'
        cs-uri-stem: '/OA_HTML/BneOfflineLOVService'
        cs-uri-query|contains: 'bne:uueupload=true'
    selection2:
        request_body|contains:
            - 'upload=@.*\.uue'
            - 'begin 777.*\.zip'
            - '\.\./'
    condition: selection1 and selection2
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative tools using UUE encoding for file transfers
level: high

attack_vector.reasoning: The write-up clearly describes an initial access vector involving a phishing email with a malicious EarthTime.exe file that triggers SectopRAT via MSBuild.exe. The attack chain is well-documented and focuses on the execution path rather than network exploitation.

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker gained initial access via a malicious EarthTime.exe file impersonating legitimate DeskSoft software, which deployed SectopRAT malware through MSBuild.exe injection. The attack chain included reconnaissance using Grixba (Play ransomware tool), SystemBC proxy tunneling, Betruger backdoor deployment, credential dumping via DCSync and Veeam database extraction, and lateral movement using RDP and PsExec. Multiple tools were used for discovery including AdFind, SharpHound, and SoftPerfect NetScan, with the threat actor leveraging masquerading techniques to disguise malware as legitimate security software.
